head: 7dc36ec (report commit; code head c950fa1)

requirements.what_changed: requirements.lock generated by scripts/lock_requirements.py from the installed closure of /home/user/Project-Money/brambleloop/.venv (33 distributions, marker/extras-aware incl. uvicorn[standard]); every pin carries all sha256 hashes PyPI publishes for that exact version (PyPI reachable via proxy). Script prints a supply-chain change record (ADDED/REMOVED/CHANGED) on regeneration and has an offline --check. Verified: a fresh python3.11 venv installs the lock with pip --require-hashes, pip check clean, core imports and tests/test_compiler.py pass in it.
requirements.live_root: Docker image build (Railway builds from Dockerfile)
requirements.remaining: The Docker build itself was not run here (no docker); verified by an equivalent --require-hashes install into a clean 3.11 venv. Change record is printed at regeneration and lives in git history of requirements.lock, not in a separate release-evidence file.

requirements.what_changed: Production dependencies now exact-pinned and hash-verified (see F-158). Removed `requests>=2.31` from requirements.txt: declared since 23ff53b but imported nowhere in src/tests/scripts and not installed in the suite venv, so the image carried an unreviewed package the suite never exercised.
requirements.remaining: Provenance/security review of repositories, binaries, services and models (beyond Python packages) is not covered; base image python:3.11-slim is tag-pinned, not digest-pinned; apt fonts-dejavu-core unpinned.

requirements.what_changed: tests/test_secret_scan.py scans every git-tracked file in the whole repo, every untracked-not-ignored file, and the ignored generated dirs (brambleloop/artifacts, brambleloop/backups, reports/shadow_release/_store, research/**/evidence) for Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS key id/secret, private keys, literal bearer tokens, Etsy OAuth tokens and keystrings, GitHub, Stripe live, Slack and passworded DB URLs. Findings print path:line, pattern and a 12-hex sha256 fingerprint, never the value. Allow-list keyed by (path, pattern, fingerprint) with a reason each; 5 entries, all deliberately fake test fixtures ('hunter2', 'wrong-token-...'). No real secret found in this tree or in the main checkout's generated dirs.
requirements.consumer: run_tests.sh full run -> run record release_eligible -> ops/deploy_guard.py
requirements.live_root: release gate: a red secret scan makes the suite red, which the deploy guard refuses
requirements.remaining: Binary files (NUL in first 8 KiB) and files >20 MB are skipped and compressed PDF streams are not decoded -- stated limits. Runtime logs outside the repo (Railway logs) are not scanned.

requirements.what_changed: src/brambleloop/ops/credential_register.py: code-held register (name, provider, held_in, exposed_at, exposure, rotate_how, rotated_at, rotation_evidence -- no value field; validate() refuses credential-shaped text). Seeded with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exposed 2026-09-19 (pasted in plaintext + screenshot, commit 3301d67). owner_requests() yields one launch.readiness.OwnerRequest per unrotated credential, key 'credential_rotation:<NAME>', in the Directive's format; rotated_at + evidence retires it. CLI `python -m brambleloop.ops.credential_register` exits 1 while rotation is required.
requirements.consumer: NOT YET WIRED: needs runtime/release.py launch assessment to add it to the owner queue (see needs_from_others)
requirements.remaining: One-line wiring into the single owner queue (runtime/release.py) and a dashboard card (app/main.py) -- both owned by other clusters.

requirements.what_changed: run_tests.sh records clean/dirty tree (git status --porcelain count) and HEAD at start and end; REQUIRE_CLEAN=1 refuses a dirty tree (exit 3); the JSON run record's release_eligible is true only for a full, clean, unmoved-HEAD, zero-failing run, and ops/deploy_guard.py accepts only such a record for the exact candidate SHA.
requirements.live_root: integrator release procedure (run REQUIRE_CLEAN=1 ./run_tests.sh, then deploy_guard check)
requirements.remaining: The full suite must actually be run with REQUIRE_CLEAN=1 on the final release candidate (integrator; not run here per brief).

requirements.what_changed: Log opens with RUN ID / RUN STARTED (UTC) / GIT SHA / TREE / SCOPE / RUN RECORD and closes with TOTAL PASSING line (unchanged format), RUN FINISHED (UTC), DURATION, GIT SHA (+tree), HEAD-moved warning, RUN RECORD -- all from git and the clock.
requirements.consumer: log readers, ops/board.py RESULT regex (TOTAL line unchanged), deploy_guard log re-derivation

requirements.what_changed: run_tests.sh writes artifacts/suite_runs/<run_id>.json (status running at start; passed/failed/interrupted at end via trap) with start/end UTC, duration, git SHA at start and end, tree state, scope, suites, suites_failing + list, tests_passing (OK), tests_failing_reported (FAIL), tests_skipped_reported (SKIP), exit code, log path, host, python, lock, release_eligible; plus a full log copy <run_id>.log. Query: `python3 ops/deploy_guard.py latest-suite [--sha X] [--eligible]` (in deploy_guard rather than registry.py, which this cluster does not own).
requirements.remaining: FAIL/SKIP counts are from column-zero markers (suite exit codes remain authoritative), labelled as such in the record.

requirements.what_changed: noclobber (O_EXCL) lock keyed by sha256(SHA|scope|interpreter realpath|hostname) under artifacts/suite_runs/locks; a second identical invocation prints the running run's lock and record and exits 75 without running anything; stale lock (pid gone or pid reused with different /proc start time) is taken over and announced; ALLOW_PARALLEL=1 is the deliberate override; lock released by the EXIT trap only if held by this run.
SUITES='a b.py tests/c.py' (spaces/commas) runs only the named suites; unknown name exits 2 having run nothing; THEN_FULL=1 chains to the full suite only if the targeted suites passed.
requirements.remaining: The targeted-first rule text in ops/HEARTBEAT_PROMPT.md (not in this cluster's ownership).

requirements.what_changed: tests/test_vacuity.py: AST scan of every tests/test_*.py flagging loops that assert over an iterable with no non-emptiness evidence in the same test (non-empty literal/range, module constant literal, UPPER_CASE code table, an assertion mentioning the iterable or a name the loop writes, or `# vacuity-ok: <reason>` for emptiness-under-test). New findings fail; 110 existing findings in other clusters' files are a shrink-only baseline keyed by (file, function, iterable source).
requirements.remaining: Fix the 110 baselined loops (add non-emptiness asserts) in files owned by other clusters; heuristic is syntactic (proves a check exists, not that it is correct).

requirements.what_changed: ops/waiter.py: O_EXCL lease per job under brambleloop/artifacts/ops_waiters/leases; a second wait for the same job ATTACHES (reads the registry verdict once, reports the live holder, exit 4) instead of polling; a lease whose holder pid is dead/reused is detected as duplicate/stale and taken over atomically.
requirements.live_root: CLI `python3 ops/waiter.py wait <job>` (operator tooling; not a runtime cadence)
requirements.remaining: Nothing forces sessions to use it instead of ad-hoc loops; HEARTBEAT_PROMPT should say so (needs_from_others).

requirements.what_changed: Every wait has max wall time (default 45 min); on breach it stops, releases its lease and returns the registry's authoritative diagnosis; live waiters are capped (default 4, exit 6 at cap); the waiter never spawns processes (asserted).
requirements.remaining: Memory/CPU of a waiter is not measured (it is a single sleeping process by construction).

requirements.what_changed: Per-operation-class durations (registry enrolment -> job's own finish stamp, deduped per run) in durations.jsonl; rolling median of last 20 with >=5 samples; a job running >3x median triggers a registry re-read with the process probe and the waiter stops if it is no longer RUNNING.
requirements.remaining: Covers operator lanes only; the product runtime's jobs table (jobs.started/finished by job_type, flagged in ops/health.py) is not covered -- cluster E owns ops/health.py.

requirements.what_changed: `ops/waiter.py ack <job>` acknowledges via Registry.acknowledge and records (ack time - job's stamped finish) as idle wall-clock in time_waste.jsonl, separate from spend; `waste` rolls up per day and raises RELIABILITY INCIDENTs (single gap >15 min or day >60 min; exit 1).
requirements.remaining: `ops/registry.py ack` itself does not account idle (not this cluster's file); the incident is not yet surfaced to the owner dashboard.

requirements.what_changed: ops/deploy_guard.py check --candidate <rev> --deployed <sha>: REFUSE unless candidate == or descends from deployed (git merge-base --is-ancestor), deployed commit known and present locally, and a release_eligible run record exists for the exact candidate SHA whose own log still names that run/SHA and says suites failing: 0. Script only; makes no network call and runs only read-only git (asserted).
requirements.live_root: integrator deploy procedure (script only; never triggers a deploy)
requirements.remaining: The deployed commit is passed in by the caller (read from production /api/verify); the guard does not fetch it (no network). No cross-session deploy lease.

tests_run.file: tests/test_compiler.py (in clean venv installed from requirements.lock with --require-hashes)

needs_from_others: runtime/release.py (launch assessment, ~line 3068): `requests = list(readiness.owner_requests()) + access.owner_requests() + credential_register.owner_requests()` so the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rotation card enters the single owner queue; keys 'credential_rotation:*' then close automatically once rotated_at is set (F-160).

Cluster E, app/main.py: surface brambleloop.ops.credential_register.report() (names/events only) as an owner card until rotated; and optionally `ops/waiter.py waste` reliability incidents (F-160, F-344).

ops/HEARTBEAT_PROMPT.md owner: add the targeted-first rule (after a hang/observer diagnosis run `SUITES=<smallest affected> ./run_tests.sh` first; full run only to prove integration, THEN_FULL=1 to chain) and require `ops/waiter.py wait` instead of ad-hoc pgrep loops, `ops/waiter.py ack` instead of `registry.py ack` (F-347, F-334, F-344).
ops/registry.py owner: optionally a `latest-suite` alias delegating to ops/deploy_guard.latest_suite, and call waiter idle accounting from Registry.acknowledge (F-345, F-344).

All clusters: tests/test_vacuity.py BASELINE lists 110 loops that assert over a possibly empty iterable in your test files; adding a non-emptiness assertion and deleting the key is required (baseline is shrink-only). Renaming a baselined test or changing the loop's iterable text makes it a NEW finding (F-123).
Cluster E / ops.health owner: product-runtime duration watchdog over jobs.started/finished by job_type (F-337 remainder).
risks: run_tests.sh was restructured (trap semantics: INT/TERM now exit 130 via the single EXIT trap; header/footer lines added around the unchanged TOTAL line; records written under artifacts/suite_runs). Its full-scope path was exercised only in a 100-dummy-suite sandbox, not on the real ~20-min suite (per brief). Integrator's first full run is the real check.

test_vacuity is merge-sensitive: other FB-1 workers adding or editing asserting loops over computed iterables will turn it red at integration; fixing a baselined loop without deleting its key also turns it red (by design).
tests/test_secret_scan.py briefly creates brambleloop/research/_secret_scan_probe/ during its run (removed in finally).

tests/test_dependency_lock.py pins lock == installed venv closure: upgrading the venv without regenerating the lock fails the suite (intended). The lock excludes test-only deps (httpx for fastapi TestClient is used by 3 suites but was never in requirements.txt), so the Docker image cannot run those suites -- pre-existing, not changed.
requests removed from requirements.txt: no import anywhere found by grep; a dynamic import would now fail in the image.
Docker build not executed here (no docker daemon); --require-hashes install verified in a clean python3.11 venv instead.
